requirement_text.REQ-059: Port src/engine/pin_resolver.zig (967 lines, R-Co's PIN-01..PIN-04) as Letflow.Engine.PinResolver -- the mechanism that freezes every versioned dependency an instance uses at start time, so a running instance is never silently upgraded by a catalog change underneath it. resolve/N (PIN-01): enumerates every versioned reference in the definition snapshot and resolves each to a PinnedVersion entry {kind, ref, resolved_id, version, source} with kind in catalog_entry | variable_schema | module and source in resolved | override | inherited. Resolution completes BEFORE the instance row is written, so a failed resolution writes no partial instance (PIN-01 AC1/AC4). pinned_versions is ordered by kind then ref, so two starts of the same definition against the same catalog produce byte-identical payloads (PIN-01 AC5) -- deterministic ordering is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Initial variables violating the resolved variable_schema version are rejected with a distinct VariableSchemaViolation-equivalent listing each failing field (PIN-01 AC3), reusing REQ-024's validator. Recording (PIN-02): the resolved pin set is written as the pinned_versions field of the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload, appended in the SAME transaction as REQ-045's instance row insert. The EVENT LOG is the record of record -- no side table stores pins (PIN-02 AC3). If the INSTANCE_STARTED append fails, the whole thing rolls back so no committed instance has an unrecorded pin set (PIN-02 AC2). A definition with zero catalog and zero module references still records exactly one variable_schema entry (PIN-02 AC4). No fallback (PIN-03): a reference with no pin entry raises a distinct PinMissing error naming the reference, and NO code path substitutes the current active version for a missing or unresolvable pin (PIN-03 AC1/AC5). A newer catalog version published mid-flight does not affect an in-flight instance (PIN-03 AC2). R-Co's PIN-03 AC4 routes an exhausted PinMissing retry budget to the dead-letter queue -- OBS-05's DLQ is S6, the same gap REQ-056 flagged; leave a named hook rather than a partial DLQ. Replay and inheritance (PIN-04): REQ-053's reconstruction reads the effective pin set from INSTANCE_STARTED plus the most recent INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event, NEVER from a live catalog (PIN-04 AC1/AC5) -- this is what makes replay deterministic. merge_effective_pins/N computes that effective set. A sub-process child instance inherits its parent's pin set and adds entries only for references the parent does not carry, with inherited entries marked source: inherited (PIN-04 AC2); a child reference resolving to a version differing from an inherited pin uses the INHERITED pin and records the conflict in the child's INSTANCE_STARTED payload (PIN-04 AC3) -- inheritance wins, which is easy to get backwards. SCOPE BOUNDARY: GET /api/v1/instances/{id}/pins (PIN-04 AC4) is S4 (api-surface); this requirement exposes the effective-pin-set function the route will call, including the source event identifier per entry. SCOPE GAP -- carry R-Co's own scoping forward explicitly rather than re-discovering it: PIN-01 AC1 (service_catalog version resolution) and AC2 (module_ref resolution against PLC-01), and PIN-03 AC3 (execution proceeds on a pinned version after that version is DEPRECATED), are NOT satisfiable in Letflow, for the same reason they are unsatisfied in R-Co itself -- R-Co holds PIN-01 and PIN-03 at TESTED rather than RELEASED over exactly this, tracked there as ISS-0672/GH-306, because service_catalog has no version/status column and PLC-01 (the process module catalog) does not exist. In Letflow the gap is wider still: src/repository/ (service_catalog) is S6 and PLC-01 is unscoped to any stage. Scope this requirement to the variable_schema branch plus the resolution/ordering/recording/inheritance MACHINERY against an injectable catalog and module lookup -- the same pattern REQ-031 used for its identical missing-catalog gap -- and have unresolvable references return distinct UnresolvedCatalogRef / UnresolvedModuleRef errors rather than a silent no-op or a stub that pretends to resolve. Name this gap in the moduledoc, with the future stage each dependency belongs to.

task.description: Design the PIN-01..04 dependency pin resolver: resolve/N's deterministic pinned-version enumeration against an injectable catalog/module/variable_schema lookup (mirroring REQ-031's already-shipped pattern for the identical missing-catalog gap), zero-partial-write integration into REQ-045's create/2 (pin resolution must complete before instance_definition_snapshots or any other row is written), variable_schema validation reusing REQ-024's JsonSchema.validate/2, PIN-03's no-fallback pin_for/3 accessor, and PIN-04's two distinct concerns -- merge_effective_pins/2 (replay-time INSTANCE_STARTED+INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND fold, for REQ-053's reconstruction) and apply_inheritance/2 (instance-start-time child pin inheritance with conflict recording). Branch feature/WF02-REQ059-20260819 already exists and is checked out (Step 00 PASSED). Read lib/letflow/engine.ex's create/2 in full (the actual shipped shape, not the spec text), lib/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator.ex (REQ-031's injectable-lookup pattern this must mirror), lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex + json_schema.ex (the REQ-024 validator to reuse), lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex (REQ-053's replay path this integrates with), and lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_plan.ex (the only existing precedent for which graph node attribute is a catalog vs. module reference) before designing. Explicitly document the SCOPE GAP (service_catalog/PLC-01 resolution deferred, citing R-Co's ISS-0672/GH-306 precedent) in the moduledoc section of the design.
acceptance_criteria: resolve returns pinned_versions ordered by kind then ref, and two resolutions of the same definition against the same injected lookups produce byte-identical output, demonstrated by an explicit test comparing serialised payloads

a failed resolution writes zero rows -- no instance_projections row, no instance_definition_snapshots row, no events row -- verified by reading all three back after a deliberately unresolvable reference
initial variables violating the resolved variable_schema are rejected with an error listing each failing field, using REQ-024's validator rather than a second implementation

the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload carries the pinned_versions entries, and a definition with zero catalog and zero module references still records exactly one variable_schema entry; no separate pin table exists anywhere in priv/repo/migrations

a reference with no pin entry returns a distinct PinMissing error naming the reference, and no code path anywhere in the module queries a catalog for a current/latest version as a fallback -- confirmed by inspection and stated in the moduledoc

a child instance started from a parent inherits the parent's pins with source: inherited, and a child reference resolving to a different version than an inherited pin uses the INHERITED version while recording the conflict in the child's INSTANCE_STARTED payload

reconstruction via REQ-053 derives the effective pin set from INSTANCE_STARTED (plus INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND when present) and issues zero reads against any catalog or module registry, demonstrated by an injected lookup that records whether it was called

the moduledoc names the service_catalog (S6) and PLC-01 (unscoped) dependency gap explicitly, cites R-Co's own ISS-0672/GH-306 precedent for holding PIN-01/PIN-03 partially unmet, and states that unresolvable references return typed errors rather than stubs

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req059-pin-resolver.md. AC mapping (design doc's own section 10 table): AC1 ordering/determinism -> section 4.3; AC2 zero-partial-write -> section 3's reordering of Engine.create/2's start_instance/5 so PinResolver.resolve/4, validate_initial_variables/2 and apply_inheritance/2 all run BEFORE create_snapshot/3 (moved earlier than the current shipped order, which today writes the snapshot row before any activation/pin code runs); AC3 variable_schema violation via REQ-024's JsonSchema.validate/2 (not Registry.validate_payload/3, a different concept) -> section 5; AC4 payload+exactly-one-variable_schema+no-pin-table -> sections 3/4.2/2; AC5 PinMissing no-fallback accessor pin_for/3 -> section 11; AC6 child inheritance+conflict recording via apply_inheritance/2 -> section 7; AC7 replay-side merge_effective_pins/2 (pure, no I/O, reusing Reconstruction.read_full_log/3 widened to public/@doc false per the established req053 OQ-2 precedent) -> section 6; AC8 SCOPE GAP citing ISS-0672/GH-306 and REQ-031's mirrored injectable-Lookup pattern -> section 2 point 2. Catalog/module reference enumeration is grounded in an existing precedent (not invented): Letflow.Definitions.PromotionPlan.build_entries/6 already defines SERVICE_TASK/service_id as the catalog dimension and SUB_PROCESS/module_ref as the module dimension for its own promotion-diff purposes; this design reuses that exact (node_type, attribute_key) pairing, cited by file/line. Six open questions listed explicitly in section 9, the most significant being OQ-1 (no R-Co source tree reachable in this environment, so pin_resolver.zig's real :override-source mechanism is an unverified inference) and OQ-2 (REQ-059's own text says reconstruction reads 'the most recent' INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event, singular, which this design deliberately diverges from -- folding ALL rebind events in sequence order instead -- since REQ-060's own delta-only per-event payload shape makes 'most recent only' lossy for multi-rebind histories; flagged for REVIEWER/REQ-060's own future designer to confirm). No implementation code included -- signatures/@spec/type shapes, event-payload JSON shapes, and the exact Engine.create/2 call-site reordering (by function name, not by body) only.
